title: Criminal Law Special Provisions Amendment Act 1974

sections.shortTitle: Criminal Law Special Provisions Amendment Act 1974
sections.description:
Short tile, extent and commencement

ACT V OF 1975
ACT V OF 1975
CRIMINAL LAW
(SPECIAL PROVISIONS) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974
An Act further to
amend the Criminal Law (Special Provisions)
Ordinance, 1968
[Gazette of
Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 17th January 1975]
The following Act of Parliament
received the assent of the President on the 13th January 1975, and is hereby
published for general, information :-
1. Short tile, extent and
commencement.----(1) This Act may be called the Criminal Law (Special
Provisions) (Amendment) Act, 1974.
(2) It extends to the areas
specified in the Schedule to the Criminal Law (Special Provisions) Ordinance,
1968 (W. P. Ordinance No. 11 of 1968).
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

sections.shortTitle: Criminal Law Special Provisions Amendment Act 1974
sections.description:
Amendment of section 5, W. P. Ordinance No. II of 1968

ACT V OF 1975
ACT V OF 1975
CRIMINAL LAW
(SPECIAL PROVISIONS) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974
An Act further to
amend the Criminal Law (Special Provisions)
Ordinance, 1968
[Gazette of
Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part I, 17th January 1975]
The following Act of Parliament
received the assent of the President on the 13th January 1975, and is hereby
published for general, information :-
2. Amendment of section 5, W.
P. Ordinance No. II of 1968.---In the Criminal Law (Special Provisions)
Ordinance, 1968 (W. P. Ordinance No. II of 1968), section 5 shall be
re-numbered as subsection (1) of that section and, alter subsection (1)
re-numbered as aforesaid, the following new subsections shall be added,
namely:-
"(2) A Tribunal shall hold
its sittings at such place as the Deputy Commissioner may fix, having regard to
the safety of the accused and the witnesses and availability of adequate legal
assistance to the accused ; and such place may also be a place situated in an
area in which this Ordinance is not for the time being in force.
(2) The power of the Deputy
Commissioner under subsection (2) shall, in respect of a place situated beyond
the jurisdiction of the Deputy Com missioner by whom the Tribunal has been
constituted, be exerciseable by the Provincial Government.".
